results.title: Strict CSP posture in BFF (spec WEB-SEC-01)
results.desc: helmet with default-src none, frame-ancestors none, self-only connect
results.detail: {"helmet-registered": true, "default-src-none": true, "frame-ancestors-none": true, "connect-src-self": true, "base-uri-none": true, "form-action-self": true}
results.prose: Random spec draw (second hit on web-console architecture - now WEB-SEC-01, browser security headers). The BFF registers @fastify/helmet with a genuinely strict CSP: default-src 'none' as the baseline, frame-ancestors 'none' (no framing), connect-src and form-action locked to 'self', base-uri disabled. This is enforcing-mode strictness, not the report-only starting posture the spec permits initially - the console's security headers are production-grade in code.
results.steps: Read bff/src/app.ts helmet config; assert default-src none, frame-ancestors none, self-scoped connect/form, base-uri none.

results.title: BFF serves compressed static assets (WEB-DPLY-02/WEB-BFF-01)
results.desc: compress + static registration in the same-origin BFF
results.prose: Sibling check on the deployment requirements: the BFF registers @fastify/compress (response compression as WEB-DPLY-02 requires for assets) and serves the built static bundle itself via @fastify/static - which is the same-origin static+API service posture WEB-BFF-01 mandates. The browser talks to one origin; static assets compressed; the architecture diagram in the spec is what the code does.
results.steps: Read bff/src/app.ts; assert compress and static registrations present.
